issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Theorem 3.3, the authors claim that the L2 error between the two bivariate trigonometric polynomials is bounded by the max-norm of their coefficient difference: \|\widetilde{F}f - Ff\|_{L^2} \le \|\mathbf{A} - \mathbf{E}\mathbf{F}^*\|_{\max}. However, under the paper's definition of the L2 inner product, the Fourier basis functions are orthonormal, so Parseval's identity gives \|\widetilde{F}f - Ff\|_{L^2} = \|\mathbf{A} - \mathbf{E}\mathbf{F}^*\|_F. In general, \|\mathbf{M}\|_F \ge \|\mathbf{M}\|_{\max}, and bounding the Frobenius norm by the max-norm requires multiplying by \sqrt{(2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)}. Therefore, Theorem 3.2 (which only bounds the max-norm error by \epsilon \|\mathbf{A}\|_2) does not bound the L2 error by \epsilon \|\mathbf{A}\|_2. Furthermore, Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 4.1 replace \min\{I_1, I_2\}^{-\alpha} from Theorem 3.1 with \max\{I_1, I_2\}^{-\alpha}, which is invalid when I_1 \neq I_2 because unresolved high frequencies in the coordinate with smaller degree do not decay with the larger degree.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must bound \|\widetilde{F}f - Ff\|_{L^2} using the Frobenius norm \|\mathbf{A} - \widetilde{\mathbf{A}}\|_F (or incorporate the dimension factor \sqrt{(2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)}, which materially worsens error and rank bounds) and replace \max\{I_1, I_2\}^{-\alpha} with \min\{I_1, I_2\}^{-\alpha}.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical error bounds for the proposed low-rank hyperinterpolation approximations in Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 4.1 are invalidated. The rigorous control over approximation quality claimed in the paper is unsubstantiated.
issues.title: False bound on L2 function error via coefficient matrix max-norm and incorrect Sobolev truncation exponent
issues.why_classification: The paper's primary theoretical error guarantees (Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 4.1) fail. A correct conversion from max-norm to Frobenius norm introduces a factor of \sqrt{(2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)} = O(\epsilon^{-1/\alpha}), which breaks convergence or materially deteriorates the advertised rank and accuracy bounds unless new proof architecture is developed.
